'''Lucie Hradecká''' ({{IPA|cs|ˈlutsɪjɛ ˈɦradɛtskaː}}; born 21 May 1985) is a Czech former professional [[tennis]] player. A three-time [[Grand Slam (tennis)|Grand Slam]] doubles champion and 26-time [[WTA Tour]] doubles titlist, she reached her career-high doubles ranking of world No. 4 in October 2012. She was also an integral member of the [[Czech Republic Billie Jean King Cup team|Czech Republic's national team]] and helped her country to win five titles at the Fed Cup (now [[Billie Jean King Cup]]) between 2011 and 2016, in addition to winning two Olympic medals in both women's doubles with [[Andrea Sestini Hlaváčková]] in [[Tennis at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Women's doubles|2012]] and in mixed doubles with [[Radek Štěpánek]] in [[Tennis at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Mixed doubles|2016]]. Hradecká also reached the top 45 in singles and was a finalist in seven tour-level singles tournaments. She announced her retirement from the sport at the end of the [[2022 WTA Tour|2022 season]].

In 2006, Hradecká won her first WTA Tour title in doubles in 2006 with partner [[Renata Voráčová]] at the [[2006 Banka Koper Slovenia Open – Doubles|Slovenia Open]]. Five years later, she made her breakthrough at the Grand Slam tournaments when she won her first of two women's doubles [[Grand Slam (tennis)|major]] titles at the [[2011 French Open – Women's doubles|2011 French Open]] with Hlaváčková. In 2012, despite losing her next two major finals, she won the silver medal at the Summer Olympics and won her first [[WTA Premier tournaments|WTA Premier 5]] (now WTA 1000) title in [[2012 Western & Southern Open – Women's doubles|Cincinnati]], both with Hlaváčková. Her continued success led her to a second major title at the [[2013 US Open – Women's doubles|US Open]] in the following year before placing runner-up at the [[2016 Australian Open – Women's doubles|2016 Australian Open]] and [[2017 US Open – Women's doubles|2017 US Open]].

Hradecká was also an accomplished mixed-doubles player, having won the [[2013 French Open – Mixed doubles|2013 French Open]] with [[František Čermák]] in addition to reaching two finals at the [[2013 Australian Open – Mixed doubles|2013 Australian Open]] (with Čermák) and the [[2015 French Open – Mixed doubles|2015 French Open]] (with [[Marcin Matkowski]]) and the mixed-doubles bronze in [[Tennis at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Mixed doubles|2016]] with Štěpánek.

In singles, Hradecká achieved her highest ranking on the WTA Tour of world No. 41 in June 2011. She reached her first final in 2008 at the [[2008 Gastein Ladies – Singles|Austrian Open]] and reached six additional finals but did not win them. Her best result at a major was at the [[2015 Australian Open – Women's singles|2015 Australian Open]], where she defeated former world No. 1, [[Ana Ivanovic]], en route to the third round.

==Career==
===2002–2008: Career beginnings, first pro tour titles===
She won her first doubles title on the WTA Tour in 2006 at [[WTA Slovenia Open|Portorož]] with partner [[Renata Voráčová]] as the fourth-seeded team. In the final, the Czech team defeated [[Eva Birnerová]] and [[Émilie Loit]], the second seeds, by walkover. They also had a victory over the top-seeds [[Maria Elena Camerin]] and [[Emmanuelle Gagliardi]] in the semifinals.

As qualifiers, she reached the third round of doubles competition with [[Hana Šromová]] at the [[2006 Wimbledon Championships – Women's doubles#Section 2|2006 Wimbledon Championships]], then lost to fifth seeds [[Meghann Shaughnessy]] and [[Anna-Lena Grönefeld]]. En route, they defeated 12th-seeds [[Svetlana Kuznetsova]] and [[Amélie Mauresmo]], the previous year's [[The Championships, Wimbledon|Wimbledon]] runner-ups by walkover.

In 2007, she made the doubles semifinals of the [[2007 Indian Wells Masters|Indian Wells Open]] tournament with Voráčová. En route, the team defeated [[Janette Husárová]] and [[Meghann Shaughnessy]], the seventh seeds, in the first round, and third-seeded [[Virginia Ruano Pascual]] and [[Paola Suárez]] in three sets in the quarterfinals, and then lost to top seeds [[Lisa Raymond]] and [[Samantha Stosur]].

Later that year, Hradecká and Voráčová won at [[Gastein Ladies|Bad Gastein]], beating [[Ágnes Szávay]] and [[Vladimíra Uhlířová]]. They also won the 2007 Portorož title, beating [[Elena Likhovtseva]] and [[Andreja Klepač]] in the finals.

Hradecká reached her first singles final at Bad Gastein in July 2008, where, as a qualifier, she got to the final, but lost to the fourth-seed [[Pauline Parmentier]] 4–6, 4–6. She also reached the doubles final.

===2009–11: 2011 French Open doubles champion, top 50 singles debut===
Hradecká  won the [[2011 Strabag Prague Open|same tournament]], defeating [[Paula Ormaechea]] in the final.

She paired with [[Andrea Hlaváčková]] to win her first Grand Slam title at the [[2011 French Open|French Open]], defeating [[Sania Mirza]] and [[Elena Vesnina]] in the final.

===2012: Wimbledon doubles final, Olympic silver medal, world No. 4===
In [[2012 Estoril Open|Estoril]], Hradecká qualified for [[2012 Mutua Madrid Open|Madrid]]. She caused the two biggest upsets in the tournament by beating the world No. 4 [[Petra Kvitová]] (who was the defending champion) and the world No. 5, Samantha Stosur on the way to her first semifinals at the Premier level, where she lost to [[Serena Williams]] in straight sets.

Hradecká and Andrea Hlaváčková reached their second Grand Slam final at Wimbledon, losing to the [[Williams sisters]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sfgate.com/sports/article/Williams-sisters-win-Wimbledon-doubles-title-3690648.php|title= Williams sisters win Wimbledon doubles title|access-date=7 July 2012 | work=San Francisco Chronicle}}</ref> Hradecká and Andrea Hlaváčková wons the silver medal in women's aboubles at the [[2012 Summer Olympics|Summer Olympics in London]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = Lucie Hradecká Bio, Stats, and Results|url = https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/hr/lucie-hradecka-1.html|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200417235446/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/hr/lucie-hradecka-1.html|url-status = dead|archive-date = 2020-04-17|website = Olympics at Sports-Reference.com|access-date = 2015-11-12}}</ref>

===2013: French Open mixed doubles champion===
Partnering [[František Čermák]], Hradecká reached the mixed doubles final at the [[2013 Australian Open – Mixed doubles|Australian Open]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/tennis/aus13/story/_/id/8886593/2013-australian-open-jarmila-gajdosova-matthew-ebden-win-mixed-doubles-title|title=Wild card entrants take title|date=27 January 2013 |publisher=ESPN|accessdate=14 July 2025}}</ref> and won the [[2013 French Open – Mixed doubles|French Open]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/tennis/french13/story/_/id/9348063/2013-french-open-lucie-hradecka-frantisek-cermak-win-mixed-doubles|title=Czech duo wins mixed doubles title|date=6 June 2013 |publisher=ESPN|accessdate=14 July 2025}}</ref>

===2015–16: Singles success, Australian Open doubles final, top 10 year-end doubles ranking===
Hradecká started 2015 ranked 141st in the world and had to qualify for the main draw of the [[2015 Australian Open|Australian Open]], which she did with three wins in the qualifying rounds. She then reached the third round, her best career showing in singles at any major.

Hradecká reached the [[2016 Australian Open]] final with Andrea Hlaváčková, losing to [[Martina Hingis]] and Sania Mirza.

===2017–22: Third US Open doubles final, retirement===
Hradecká reached another final at the [[2017 US Open (tennis)|2017 US Open]] with Kateřina Siniaková, losing to Hingis and [[Chan Yung-jan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.firstpost.com/sports/us-open-2017-martina-hingis-and-chan-yung-jan-clinch-womens-doubles-title-with-comfortable-win-4029901.html|title=US Open 2017: Martina Hingis and Chan Yung-Jan clinch women's doubles title with comfortable win|date=11 September 2017 |publisher=Firstpost|accessdate=22 November 2024}}</ref>

She announced her final retirement in doubles in October 2022. Her last match was at the [[2022 Guadalajara Open Akron|Guadalajara Open]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://lastwordonsports.com/tennis/2022/10/20/lucie-hradecka-plays-final-match-of-accomplished-doubles-career-in-guadalajara/ | title=Lucie Hradecka Plays Final Match of Accomplished Doubles Career in Guadalajara | date=20 October 2022 }}</ref>
